title: A carried, still-running Codex test is not counted as a running command when a later turn's check starts
outcome: A check started while a carried Codex test of the same session is still running in the same worktree is marked overlapped, with that carried test named as still running, so it cannot be credited while the earlier process may still write ignored artifacts or build outputs it reads. The cheap fix: when a check starts, treat each carried, unended (end not reported) Codex test of the session in that worktree as a running command, giving the overlap cause "<the carried test> was still running".
acceptance: A regression test carries Codex test A into the next turn and starts test B in the same worktree, B finishing before A ends: B is marked overlapped with A named as still running, and earns no verification credit.
A check started after the carried test's end was reported is not marked overlapped by it.

The full gate passes on the exact committed tree: the host-recorded passed full-gate test verification for that tree, recorded on w-67d248c998ef (which lands in the same commit), is cited in a holder note on this item with its record id, source revision and run id, and that source revision matches this item's judged revision.
